CDF Difference-in-Differences for a Single 2x2 Cell

Source: R/cdf_did.R
cdf_did_gt.Rd

Computes the ATT and the distributions needed for the QTT for one group-time cell under parallel trends in the distribution functions of untreated potential outcomes. Used as the attgt_fun in pte by cdf_did.

Usage

cdf_did_gt(gt_data, xformula = ~1, est_method = c("aipw", "ipw", "reg"), ...)

Arguments

gt_data

A gt_data_frame for one (g,t) cell, as produced by ptetools::two_by_two_subset (panel) or ptetools::two_by_two_rcs_subset (repeated cross sections), with columns Y, D, name, id, .w and any covariates.

xformula

One-sided formula of covariates. Default ~1.

est_method

With covariates: "aipw" (default, doubly robust), "ipw", or "reg" (outcome regression). Ignored without covariates.

...

Additional arguments passed by ptetools; ignored.

Value

A ptetools::attgt_noif object with the ATT and, in extra_gt_returns, F0 (rearranged counterfactual distribution), F1 (treated post-period distribution), Fte = NULL, and cdf_violation.

Details

The counterfactual distribution of untreated outcomes for the treated group in the post period is $$F_{0}(y) = F_{\text{pre},D=1}(y) + F_{\text{post},D=0}(y) - F_{\text{pre},D=0}(y),$$ evaluated exactly at every point of the pooled support of the three distributions on the right. The raw \(F_0\) need not be a valid distribution function (it can decrease, or leave 0, 1); it is made one by monotone rearrangement (sorting its values; Chernozhukov, Fernandez-Val and Galichon 2010) and clipping to 0, 1. The largest change this makes is returned as cdf_violation; large values are evidence against the identifying assumption.

The ATT is the mean of the treated group's observed post-period outcomes minus the mean of the raw \(F_0\), which is what the assumption identifies. Without covariates this equals the usual DiD ATT.

With covariates, the comparison group's change in CDFs is averaged over the treated group's covariate distribution. For each \(y\) this is a DiD for the outcome \(1\{Y \le y\}\), estimated as in Sant'Anna and Zhao (2020): by outcome regression (distribution regression of \(1\{Y \le y\}\) on the covariates, in each period), by inverse probability weighting, or doubly robust (AIPW, the default). IPW is exact on the data's support points; outcome regression and AIPW use the distribution regression's threshold grid (see cic_gt's cond_dist = "dr"). The propensity score is a weighted logit of treatment on the pre-period covariates.

The distribution of individual treatment effects is not identified, so Fte is NULL.

References

Roth, Jonathan, and Pedro H. C. Sant'Anna. “When Is Parallel Trends Sensitive to Functional Form?” Econometrica 91(2), pp. 737-747, 2023.

Sant'Anna, Pedro H. C., and Jun Zhao. “Doubly Robust Difference-in-Differences Estimators.” Journal of Econometrics 219(1), pp. 101-122, 2020.

Chernozhukov, Victor, Ivan Fernandez-Val, and Alfred Galichon. “Quantile and Probability Curves Without Crossing.” Econometrica 78(3), pp. 1093-1125, 2010.
